sources.title: ASIC Company Dataset, October 2026 release: extract of the companies behind NSW data centre applications
sources.notes: ASIC's whole company register, published monthly under CC BY 3.0 AU: each company's name, ACN, type, status and registration date, and for a renamed company each former name with the date the current one took effect. No directors, shareholders or addresses. Downloaded 2026-10-21 (ZIP SHA-256 in the manifest) and filtered by scrapers/fetch_asic_companies.py to 185 rows, committed at data/raw/asic/company_dataset_202610_extract.csv. Names only: who owns a company needs a paid extract (docs/requests/PAID-SEARCHES.md). PROCESS NOTE (2026-10-22): data.gov.au's robots.txt, read that day, disallows every crawler; the fetcher did not read it before this download and now refuses. Whether this extract stays is for the author.

sources.title: NSW Government backs data centre investment, sets course for sustainable development (ministerial media release, 27 March 2026)
sources.publisher: NSW Government - Treasurer, Minister for Industry and Trade, Minister for Planning and Public Spaces
sources.notes: Names the proponent, project and local government area for all 15 data centre projects endorsed in Round 1 of the Investment Delivery Authority (IDA), collectively worth $51.9bn. Also records that the IDA did NOT endorse around $40.7bn of data centre and technology proposals considered premature or overly speculative; that 90 data centres are operating in NSW; that data centre investment has grown 65% per year on average over three years; that data centres are 12% of all non-residential building investment in NSW; that eight data centre projects worth more than $10bn were approved in the past year including the biggest in the Southern Hemisphere; and that one further endorsed project is withheld for commercial sensitivity. This is the authoritative proponent list for the NSW pipeline. ARCHIVED 2026-10-21 at data/raw/operators/nswgov/ with a SHA-256 manifest.

insert.notes: Of the 22 determined NSW data centre State Significant Development consents whose Department assessment report is archived (batch S2; the Dicker Data warehouse is excluded as not a data centre), 9 describe the applicant as acting for, or approached by, a data centre operator the report does not name: Lane Cove West (SSD-9741, Greenbox Architecture), Macquarie Park (SSD-10467, Stockland Trust Management), Station Road (SSD-33781208, Lehr), Kemps Creek (SSD-10101987, Arup; the end user is identified only by 'the asset numbers SYD05, 06 & 07'), 51 Huntingwood Drive (SSD-41589232, EMKC Cubed Management), Project Echidna (SSD-47320208, ARUP Australia), Davis Road (SSD-59416728, Cundall), Apollo Place (SSD-67407231, EMKC Cubed Management) and 43-61 Turner Road (SSD-68013714, ARUP). One more names a consultancy applicant without mentioning an operator at all (Glendenning Road, SSD-73761707, Lehr). Four name a property developer that builds for tenants it does not name (Goodman for Project Pluto, Project Duke and Project Apollo; Stockland for 1-5 Khartoum Road). Eight name the operator itself: CDC (Roberts Road, Marsden Park), NineZero (the Eastern Creek expansion, and DCI Poplars, 'trading as DCI Data Centers'), Macquarie Data Centres (Talavera Road), Equinix (Grand Avenue), NEXTDC (S4) and HDI SYD1, which the report calls DigiCo (SYD1). So 14 of 22 consents went to an applicant that is not the operator. Read 2026-10-21 by scripts/curate_who_applies.py; each of the nine is quoted in this row's source references.

set.notes: RESOLVED 2026-10-22 from ASIC's Company Dataset (SRC_ASIC_COMPANIES_202610), with a correction. Registration dates for the companies holding the 21 determined consents whose applicant is a company (trusts are not on the register), and how long each had existed when its consent was determined: Greenbox Architecture Pty Ltd 01/10/2009 for SSD-9741 (10.1 years); Canberra Data Centres Pty Ltd 31/05/2007 for SSD-10330 (13.1 years); Stockland Trust Management Limited 15/05/1980 for SSD-10467 (41.0 years); Lehr Consultants International (Australia) Pty Ltd 23/02/2007 for SSD-33781208 (15.8 years); Arup Pty Ltd 06/01/1972 for SSD-10101987 (51.5 years); NineZero DC Sub TC I Pty Ltd 13/08/2015 for SSD-21342738 (8.1 years); EMKC Cubed Management Pty Ltd 11/05/2021 for SSD-41589232 (2.3 years); Macquarie Data Centres Pty Ltd 06/05/2016 for SSD-24299707 (7.7 years); ARUP Australia Pty Ltd 02/05/2018 for SSD-47320208 (5.9 years); Equinix Hyperscale 2 (SY10) Pty Limited 26/07/2021 for SSD-53338465 (3.4 years); Cundall Johnston and Partners Pty Ltd 30/05/2003 for SSD-59416728 (21.6 years); EMKC Cubed Management Pty Ltd 11/05/2021 for SSD-67407231 (4.4 years); ARUP Pty Ltd 06/01/1972 for SSD-68013714 (53.9 years); CDC Data Centres Pty Ltd 31/05/2007 for SSD-70889211 (18.5 years); Goodman Property Services (Aust) Pty Limited 06/08/1999 for SSD-71368959 (26.4 years); HDI SYD1 Property Holdings Limited 07/08/2000 for SSD-69637456 (25.4 years); NEXTDC Limited 11/05/2010 for SSD-63741210 (15.6 years); Stockland Development Pty Limited 21/08/1947 for SSD-63235720 (78.6 years); Goodman Property Services (Aust) Pty Ltd 06/08/1999 for SSD-69223466 (27.0 years); Goodman Property Services (Aust) Pty Limited 06/08/1999 for SSD-74069708 (27.1 years); Lehr Consultants International (Australia) Pty Ltd 23/02/2007 for SSD-73761707 (19.6 years). Only one was under three years old: EMKC Cubed Management Pty Ltd (SSD-41589232, 2.3 years). So the claim in this question's earlier notes, that the legal person carrying a consent is usually a purpose-built entity with no operating history, does not hold: most consent holders are long-established consultancies, developers and operators. The pattern the assessment reports show is different: in 9 of 22 consents an established consultancy or developer applies for an operator the report does not name (metric nsw_dc_consents_applicant_acts_for_unnamed_operator). Fresh vehicles do appear in the newest and largest proposals, which are not yet determined: KNBDC SYD4 Pty Ltd (Mamre Road, registered 10 June 2025, now AirTrunk SYD4), WDDP Pty Ltd (Western Downs, 28 July 2026) and Project Garden 1 Pty Ltd (Brookhollow Avenue, 3 February 2025).

ADVANCED 2026-10-22. ASIC's register shows KNBDC SYD4 Pty Ltd (ACN 687 904 963, registered 10 June 2025) has been named AirTrunk SYD4 Pty Ltd since 16 June 2026, as have its Hold, Intermediate Hold, FinCo and Financing Holdco companies, so the AirTrunk link this question asked about is now on a primary record. The title search filed with the EIS shows Lot 10 DP 1280592 registered to ISPT Pty Limited (named IFM Real Estate Fiduciary Pty Ltd since 24 November 2025) with a caveat by KNBDC SYD4 Pty Ltd. The landowner's consent letters from IFM, GPT and Gibb Group are restricted on the portal. Still open: shareholders, directors and ultimate parent, which need a paid ASIC extract (docs/requests/PAID-SEARCHES.md), and what interest the caveat protects.
